who: Social historian of Sweden at Memorial University of Newfoundland; PhD Carnegie Mellon, 2000.

evidence.says: Memorial lists Stephan Curtis as an associate professor researching Swedish and European social and medical history, with a Carnegie Mellon PhD (2000).
The candidate authority identifies Stanley James Curtis, reader in Education at the University of Leeds (1955–1958) and author of Education in Britain since 1900 (1952).

notes: Stephan Curtis and Stanley James Curtis have different names, institutions, fields and career periods.

who: Historian of indigenous North America; formerly University of California, Santa Barbara, subsequently Oxford; doctorate Helsinki.

evidence.says: UCSB lists Pekka Hämäläinen (Oxford) among the faculty advisors of Jackson Warkentin’s The Iroquois Century, matching the supplied dissertation.
Oxford’s March 2012 staff magazine announces Hämäläinen’s move from UCSB and states that he completed his PhD at Helsinki.
The candidate authority identifies Pekka Hämäläinen as a UCSB professor of Spanish Borderlands and Native American History, later an Oxford professor and author of Lakota America.

notes: Direct advisor evidence confirms the candidate. The supplied Indiana doctorate (1966) conflicts with the independently documented Helsinki doctorate and appears misattached.

who: Thomas Howard, history professor at the University of North Dakota.

evidence.says: The North Dakota University System describes Thomas Howard as a UND history professor and colleague of Jerome Tweton.
The candidate is Thomas Albert Howard, a historian affiliated with Gordon College and Valparaiso, with a University of Virginia PhD (1996) in European intellectual history.
Valparaiso’s faculty roster lists Thomas Albert Howard’s BA (1990), MA (1992) and University of Virginia PhD (1996).

notes: The candidate’s education and career belong to a later period than the UND supervisor of the 1974 dissertation and do not match the supplied Florida State doctorate (1965).

who: Medieval historian at University of California, Berkeley; PhD Stanford, 1982.

evidence.says: Berkeley lists Geoffrey Koziol’s Stanford PhD (1982), medieval research interests, and Berkeley appointments beginning in 1989.
Daniel Melleno’s 2014 Berkeley dissertation names Geoffrey Koziol as advisor and committee chair.
The candidate authority identifies Geoffrey Koziol of Berkeley’s History Department, author of Begging Pardon and Favor (1992).

notes: Name, institution, doctorate and direct student-advisor evidence agree. The repository gives Melleno’s final dissertation title as Before They Were Vikings, differing from the supplied AHA title.

who: John Sherwood, historian at Queen’s University, Canada, during the 1970s.

evidence.says: The Canada Council’s 1974 report lists John Sherwood at Queen’s in History.
The Naval History and Heritage Command identifies its historian John Sherwood as holding a Columbia MA (1991) and George Washington University history doctorate (1995).
The candidate authority identifies John Darrell Sherwood as the author of Officers in Flight Suits (1996).

notes: The candidate is the later naval historian, whose doctorate and career do not match the Queen’s advisor of the 1978 dissertation. Columbia was the candidate’s MA institution, not his PhD institution.

who: Franklin Walker, historian at Loyola University Chicago.

evidence.says: The AHA’s 1959 meeting program lists Franklin Walker of Loyola University on its local arrangements committee.
The candidate authority identifies Francis Amasa Walker, author of The Wages Question and a professor of political economy and history at Yale.
MIT’s historical list identifies Francis Amasa Walker as its president during 1881–1897.

notes: Franklin Walker at Loyola and the nineteenth-century economist Francis Amasa Walker are different people; the candidate cannot be the advisor of the 1971 dissertation.

who: Mary Frank Fox, sociologist of science at Georgia Institute of Technology; PhD sociology, Michigan, 1978.

evidence.says: Georgia Tech’s repository identifies Mary Frank Fox as advisor of Irina Nikiforova’s 2012 Turing Award Scientists dissertation, matching the supplied student and title.
Fox’s institutional biography identifies her as a Georgia Tech professor researching science and academia, with a Michigan sociology PhD (1978).
The candidate authority is Fox, Mary Frank, associated with the University of Michigan and the works Women at Work (1984) and Scholarly Writing and Publishing (1985).

notes: The dissertation explicitly supplies the fuller name, selecting Mary Frank Fox from the candidates. The supplied Notre Dame history doctorate (1950) conflicts with her documented Michigan sociology doctorate and appears misattached.

who: Simon P. Fullinwider, history professor at Arizona State University.

evidence.says: ASU’s retirees association identifies Simon P. Fullinwider as an emeritus professor in the ASU History Department.
The candidate authority identifies Simon Peter Fullinwider, a naval commander associated with The Northern Barrage and Other Mining Activities (1920), and a Naval Academy graduate of 1894.
A Navy documentary history identifies Commander Simon P. Fullinwider of the Bureau of Ordnance as the author of a 1917 memorandum on the North Sea Barrage.

notes: The candidate is an earlier naval officer, distinct from the ASU history professor who supervised the 1978 dissertation.
